description: Bellman-Ford finds shortest paths from one source in a graph whose edge weights can be negative. It relaxes every edge in passes: an edge `u → v` of weight `w` lowers the distance of `v` to `d(u) + w` when that is smaller. With `n` vertices, all distances are final after `n − 1` passes, so a change in pass `n` proves a *negative cycle* (a cycle whose weights add up to less than zero). A simple temporal network (STN) turns each constraint `lo ≤ t_j − t_i ≤ hi` into two such edges, and it is *consistent* (some schedule meets every constraint) exactly when this graph has no negative cycle. `temporal-control` starts all distances at zero and returns either the distances as a valid schedule or the negative cycle as a list of constraint bounds.

papers.authors: Rina Dechter, Itay Meiri, Judea Pearl
papers.title: Temporal constraint networks
